options.text: A server that stores and distributes images, which you push to and pull from
The writable layer of a container

questions.explanation: A registry stores and distributes images. Docker Hub is the default public registry; GHCR and cloud/self-hosted registries are common alternatives.

questions.prompt: To push an image to GitHub Container Registry, how must it be named?
questions.explanation: A registry-qualified name like ghcr.io/owner/repo:tag tells docker push which registry and repository to upload to.

questions.prompt: Does docker tag copy the image?

options.text: Yes, it makes a full duplicate
No, it only adds another name pointing at the same image
Only for images larger than 1 GB
Only when pushing to Docker Hub

questions.explanation: docker tag adds an additional reference to an existing image without copying it. One image can carry many tags simultaneously.

questions.prompt: The strongest way to guarantee you deploy an exact, unchanging image is to reference it by its ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: A digest (repo@sha256:...) is immutable and always resolves to the identical image bytes, even if tags are later moved.

questions.prompt: Which are good tagging or registry practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tag releases with a specific semantic version
Add a git-SHA tag in CI for traceability
Authenticate with a scoped token passed via --password-stdin
Deploy :latest to production as the source of truth

questions.explanation: Pin versions, add SHA tags for traceability, and use scoped tokens safely. latest is a moving label and should not be the production source of truth.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to publish a local image to a registry.

items.text: docker tag the image with a registry-qualified name
A teammate pulls it by that name or digest

questions.explanation: Authenticate, give the image a registry-qualified name, push it, and then it can be pulled by others.
